subject: Request: Short-term pilot credit to preserve evaluation during procurement audit
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healco.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot access pause — procurement audit hold

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from procurement — our finance/audit team has flagged the vendor intake for a routine review and they’ve put all new contracts on hold while they complete it. We’re right in the middle of evaluating Redwood and our engineers were about to run a deeper set of workload tests this week.

I don’t expect the audit to take more than ~10 business days, but the current trial window will expire before then. Is there a way to preserve our environment / extend the pilot so we don’t lose the state and test results? We can expedite the paperwork on our side but need a short-term workaround.

Thanks,
Elena Morales\Director of Engineering\HealCo

---
attachments: pilot-usage-report.csv (csv)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healco.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot access pause — procurement audit hold

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the timing. We can absolutely help keep your environment live while procurement completes the audit. Two quick options we commonly offer: a) a short pilot extension (7–14 days) or b) a temporary token/credit allocation so your team can finish the tests without spinning up new resources.

Can you confirm roughly how many GPU-hours or token usage you expect to need to finish the workload? If you’re not sure, we can start with a conservative safety-net (I’m proposing 1,000 compute-units / tokens) and adjust once we see short-term consumption.

I’m looping in Soojin (Sales Ops) and Grace (Customer Success) to expedite approval and make the change on our side. If that works, I’ll send an approval note back to you with the exact top-up and new expiry date.

Best,
Karthik Iyer\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference

---
attachments: HealCo-SOW-draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot access pause — procurement audit hold

Karthik — fine to approve a modest safety-net for HealCo to finish the tests. Approving 1,000 compute-units (internal SKU: TRIAL-1000) and a 10-calendar-day extension to the pilot environment. Please confirm no additional billing action required and that we mark this as a one-time bridge amount tied to deal HC-2025-09-14-01.

Also note: CS will follow up to capture any updated requirements and ensure demos and test results are captured in the account record.

Thanks,
Soojin
Sales Operations\Redwood Inference

Elena — following up with the approved details. Per Soojin’s sign-off we’ve applied a one-time safety-net to your account: 1,000 compute-units (TRIAL-1000) and extended the pilot expiry by 10 calendar days. The credit will appear on your account immediately and is scoped to the current project/testing workspace.

Practical notes:
- New expiry: 2025-09-27 23:59 PDT
- Credit: 1,000 compute-units (non-billable; one-time)
- No automatic conversion to paid services — we’ll wait for your procurement approval before any changes to billing.
- CS (Grace) will schedule a quick checkpoints call to capture test artifacts and help prioritize rollout tasks once the audit clears.

Attached: updated SOW draft (minor wording to reflect temporary credit) and the pilot usage snapshot you sent. If procurement needs a formal note from us, happy to provide a short email confirming the environment hold and temporary credit allocation.

Thanks and good luck with the audit — reach out if anything changes.

Best,
Karthik Iyer\Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference
